result.title: Score-based Black-box Attack via Adversarial Condition Guided Diffusion Model
result.summary: Generative models enable unrestricted adversarial attacks that aim to fool classifiers while preserving the natural appearance and semantics of the original image. However, existing diffusion-based black-box attacks largely rely on transferability from surrogates, making their effectiveness sensitive to differences between surrogate and victim. Improving transferability can also distort semantic content and degrade image quality. Moreover, retaining the original prompt to preserve fidelity leaves the diffusion model's conditional prior underused for adversarial guidance. We address these limitations by adapting score-based black-box attacks to reverse diffusion, using the victim's output probabilities to guide latent updates without accessing its gradients. We further introduce adaptive-target guidance, which uses the victim's current runner-up class as an adversarial condition to steer denoising towards the decision boundary. Because such guidance can introduce unwanted semantic changes, we also propose target-search guidance, which searches for a small perturbation of the original condition embedding using a score-based attack. This achieves comparable attack effectiveness with better image quality than runner-up guidance. Experiments on the ImageNet-Compatible dataset show that our framework outperforms transfer-based baselines in both attack effectiveness and image quality.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出一种基于分数的黑盒对抗攻击框架，在反向扩散过程中用受害者模型的输出概率引导 latent 更新，并加入自适应目标引导与目标搜索引导以逼近决策边界、同时保持图像质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 用外部模型反馈闭环更新扩散 latent、并以搜索方式扰动条件嵌入，可能为 LVR 中测试期 latent 状态引导与视觉证据筛选提供可核查线索；但论文目标是攻击分类器与保真度，与视觉推理无直接关联，需较多人工判断。
